questions.q: An aromatic hydrocarbon $X$ with molecular formula $\text{C}_8\text{H}_{10}$ is oxidized by hot alkaline $\text{KMnO}_4$ followed by acidification to give an aromatic carboxylic acid $Y$. Nitration of $Y$ with $\text{HNO}_3/\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ gives a major product $Z$. If $Z$ contains exactly $5$ $\pi$-bonds, the number of possible structural isomers for hydrocarbon $X$ is
questions.question: An aromatic hydrocarbon $X$ with molecular formula $\text{C}_8\text{H}_{10}$ is oxidized by hot alkaline $\text{KMnO}_4$ followed by acidification to give an aromatic carboxylic acid $Y$. Nitration of $Y$ with $\text{HNO}_3/\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ gives a major product $Z$. If $Z$ contains exactly $5$ $\pi$-bonds, the number of possible structural isomers for hydrocarbon $X$ is
questions.solution:
The structural isomers of $\text{C}_8\text{H}_{10}$ containing a benzene ring are ethylbenzene, $o$-xylene, $m$-xylene, and $p$-xylene.

Oxidation of ethylbenzene with hot alkaline $\text{KMnO}_4$ followed by acidification yields benzoic acid. Nitration of benzoic acid yields $m$-nitrobenzoic acid as the major product. The number of $\pi$-bonds in $m$-nitrobenzoic acid is $3$ (benzene ring) $+ 1$ ($-\text{COOH}$ group) $+ 1$ ($-\text{NO}_2$ group) $= 5$.

Oxidation of the xylenes ($o$-, $m$-, and $p$-) yields the corresponding benzenedicarboxylic acids (phthalic, isophthalic, and terephthalic acids). Nitration of these dicarboxylic acids yields mononitro derivatives. The number of $\pi$-bonds in these products is $3$ (benzene ring) $+ 2$ (two $-\text{COOH}$ groups) $+ 1$ ($-\text{NO}_2$ group) $= 6$.

Thus, only ethylbenzene satisfies the condition. The number of possible structural isomers for $X$ is $1$.

Answer: $1$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When 2-allylphenol is treated with $\text{I}_2$ in the presence of $\text{NaHCO}_3$, the major organic product formed is:
questions.question: When 2-allylphenol is treated with $\text{I}_2$ in the presence of $\text{NaHCO}_3$, the major organic product formed is:
questions.solution:
The reaction is an intramolecular iodoetherification.

First, iodine reacts with the double bond of the allyl group to form a cyclic iodonium ion intermediate.

The phenolic oxygen then acts as an internal nucleophile. According to Baldwin's rules, the 5-exo-tet cyclization is kinetically favored over the 6-endo-tet cyclization.

Thus, the oxygen attacks the internal carbon of the iodonium ion, opening the three-membered ring to form a five-membered oxygen-containing ring.

The base ($\text{NaHCO}_3$) neutralizes the protons generated during the reaction. The final major product is 2-(iodomethyl)-2,3-dihydrobenzofuran.

Answer: 2-(Iodomethyl)-2,3-dihydrobenzofuran

questions.q: An isomer X of molecular formula $\text{C}_8\text{H}_9\text{Br}$ is found to be optically active. It is reacted with magnesium in dry ether, followed by treatment with $\text{CO}_2$ and subsequent acidic hydrolysis to yield compound Y. Compound Y is then treated with $\text{Br}_2$ in the presence of red phosphorus to give compound Z as the major product. The structure of compound Z is:
questions.question: An isomer X of molecular formula $\text{C}_8\text{H}_9\text{Br}$ is found to be optically active. It is reacted with magnesium in dry ether, followed by treatment with $\text{CO}_2$ and subsequent acidic hydrolysis to yield compound Y. Compound Y is then treated with $\text{Br}_2$ in the presence of red phosphorus to give compound Z as the major product. The structure of compound Z is:
questions.solution:
The molecular formula of X is $\text{C}_8\text{H}_9\text{Br}$. Since X is optically active, it must possess a chiral center. The only isomer of $\text{C}_8\text{H}_9\text{Br}$ with a chiral center is 1-bromoethylbenzene, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{CH}(\text{Br})-\text{CH}_3$.

Reaction of X with Mg in dry ether forms the Grignard reagent, which upon reaction with $\text{CO}_2$ followed by acidic hydrolysis yields the carboxylic acid Y. Thus, Y is 2-phenylpropanoic acid, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{COOH}$.

Treatment of Y with $\text{Br}_2$ and red phosphorus is the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction, which results in the bromination of the $\alpha$-carbon of the carboxylic acid.

The $\alpha$-carbon in Y has one hydrogen atom, which is replaced by bromine to form 2-bromo-2-phenylpropanoic acid (Z). Therefore, the structure of Z is $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{C}(\text{Br})(\text{CH}_3)-\text{COOH}$.

Answer: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{C}(\text{Br})(\text{CH}_3)-\text{COOH}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following carboxylic acids, when its vapours are passed over heated $\text{MnO}$ at $300^\circ\text{C}$, yields propanone as the major product?
questions.question: Which of the following carboxylic acids, when its vapours are passed over heated $\text{MnO}$ at $300^\circ\text{C}$, yields propanone as the major product?
options: An equimolar mixture of ethanoic acid and methanoic acid
questions.solution:
When the vapours of a carboxylic acid are passed over heated $\text{MnO}$ at $300^\circ\text{C}$, catalytic decomposition occurs to form a symmetrical ketone.

The general reaction is:
$2\text{RCOOH} \xrightarrow{\text{MnO}, 300^\circ\text{C}} \text{R-CO-R} + \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

To obtain propanone ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$), the alkyl group $\text{R}$ must be a methyl group ($\text{CH}_3$).

Thus, the required carboxylic acid is ethanoic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$).

Answer: Ethanoic acid

questions.q:
An aromatic hydrocarbon X having the molecular formula $\text{C}_9\text{H}_{12}$ is heated with alkaline $\text{KMnO}_4$ followed by acidification to yield a dicarboxylic acid Y. Compound Y undergoes electrophilic bromination with $\text{Br}_2$ in the presence of $\text{FeBr}_3$ to yield only a single monobrominated product.
The number of benzylic hydrogen atoms in compound X is _______.
questions.question:
An aromatic hydrocarbon X having the molecular formula $\text{C}_9\text{H}_{12}$ is heated with alkaline $\text{KMnO}_4$ followed by acidification to yield a dicarboxylic acid Y. Compound Y undergoes electrophilic bromination with $\text{Br}_2$ in the presence of $\text{FeBr}_3$ to yield only a single monobrominated product.
The number of benzylic hydrogen atoms in compound X is _______.
questions.solution:
(i) Oxidation of hydrocarbon X ($\text{C}_9\text{H}_{12}$) yields a dicarboxylic acid (Y). This indicates the presence of two alkyl side chains on the benzene ring.

(ii) The remaining 3 carbon atoms (since the benzene ring accounts for 6) must be distributed as a methyl group ($-\text{CH}_3$) and an ethyl group ($-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$).

(iii) Compound Y is a benzenedicarboxylic acid. Since it yields only a single monobrominated product upon electrophilic aromatic substitution, all four available positions on its benzene ring must be equivalent due to symmetry.

(iv) This symmetry is only possible for benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid (terephthalic acid).

(v) Therefore, the original hydrocarbon X must be 1-ethyl-4-methylbenzene.

(vi) In 1-ethyl-4-methylbenzene, the methyl group has 3 benzylic hydrogen atoms and the ethyl group has 2 benzylic hydrogen atoms (on the $-\text{CH}_2-$ carbon attached directly to the ring).

Total number of benzylic hydrogen atoms $= 3 + 2 = 5$.

Answer: $5$

questions.q: When an equimolar mixture of benzoic acid and ethanoic acid is passed over heated $\text{MnO}$ at $300^\circ\text{C}$, it yields a major cross-product $\text{P}$. Compound $\text{P}$ is then treated with a mixture of $\text{I}_2$ and $\text{NaOH}$. The final products obtained are:
questions.question: When an equimolar mixture of benzoic acid and ethanoic acid is passed over heated $\text{MnO}$ at $300^\circ\text{C}$, it yields a major cross-product $\text{P}$. Compound $\text{P}$ is then treated with a mixture of $\text{I}_2$ and $\text{NaOH}$. The final products obtained are:
questions.solution:
\text{COOH} + \text{CH}_3\text{COOH} \xrightarrow{\text{MnO}, 300^\circ\text{C}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3 + \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

Acetophenone ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3$) contains a methyl ketone group ($-\text{COCH}_3$), so it undergoes the haloform reaction when treated with $\text{I}_2$ and $\text{NaOH}$.

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3 + 3\text{I}_2 + 4\text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COONa} + \text{CHI}_3 + 3\text{NaI} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$

Therefore, the final products are sodium benzoate ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COONa}$) and iodoform ($\text{CHI}_3$).

Answer: Sodium benzoate and iodoform

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An acyclic unsaturated carboxylic acid 'X' reacts with $\text{I}_2$ and $\text{NaHCO}_3$ to give 5-(1-iodoethyl)dihydrofuran-2(3H)-one as the major product. The IUPAC name of 'X' is:
questions.question: An acyclic unsaturated carboxylic acid 'X' reacts with $\text{I}_2$ and $\text{NaHCO}_3$ to give 5-(1-iodoethyl)dihydrofuran-2(3H)-one as the major product. The IUPAC name of 'X' is:
questions.solution:
The formation of a lactone from an unsaturated carboxylic acid using $\text{I}_2$ and $\text{NaHCO}_3$ proceeds via an iodolactonization reaction.

The product is a five-membered $\gamma$-lactone (dihydrofuran-2(3H)-one) with a 1-iodoethyl group at the 5-position.

In the lactone ring, the oxygen is bonded to what was the carbonyl carbon (C1) and the $\gamma$-carbon (C4) of the original acid. This indicates that the nucleophilic attack of the carboxylate occurred at C4, which means the original double bond was between C4 and C5.

The substituent at the ring carbon (C5 of the lactone, which was C4 of the acid) is a $-\text{CH}(\text{I})\text{CH}_3$ group, meaning the original chain had six carbons with the double bond at C4.

Thus, the starting material 'X' is hex-4-enoic acid.

Answer: Hex-4-enoic acid

Consider the following reaction sequence:
$CH_3CH_2CH_2C\equiv N \xrightarrow{H_3O^+/\Delta} \text{X} \xrightarrow[\text{(ii) } H_2O]{\text{(i) } Br_2/\text{Red P}} \text{Y} \xrightarrow{\text{alc. } KOH, \Delta} \text{Z (Major product)}$
The IUPAC name of the major product 'Z' is:
questions.question:
Consider the following reaction sequence:
$CH_3CH_2CH_2C\equiv N \xrightarrow{H_3O^+/\Delta} \text{X} \xrightarrow[\text{(ii) } H_2O]{\text{(i) } Br_2/\text{Red P}} \text{Y} \xrightarrow{\text{alc. } KOH, \Delta} \text{Z (Major product)}$
The IUPAC name of the major product 'Z' is:
questions.solution:
Step 1: Complete hydrolysis of butanenitrile under acidic conditions yields butanoic acid.
$CH_3CH_2CH_2C\equiv N \xrightarrow{H_3O^+/\Delta} CH_3CH_2CH_2COOH$ (X)

Step 2: Butanoic acid undergoes the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction with bromine and red phosphorus, which selectively substitutes an $\alpha$-hydrogen with bromine to form $2$-bromobutanoic acid.
$CH_3CH_2CH_2COOH \xrightarrow[\text{(ii) } H_2O]{\text{(i) } Br_2/\text{Red P}} CH_3CH_2CH(Br)COOH$ (Y)

Step 3: Treatment of an $\alpha$-halo acid with alcoholic $KOH$ and heat causes dehydrohalogenation (an $E2$ elimination). The $\alpha$-bromine and a $\beta$-hydrogen are removed to form a conjugated double bond, yielding but-$2$-enoic acid.
$CH_3CH_2CH(Br)COOH \xrightarrow{\text{alc. } KOH, \Delta} CH_3-CH=CH-COOH$ (Z)
Thus, the major product 'Z' is but-$2$-enoic acid.

Answer: But-$2$-enoic acid

(A) Propanoic acid
(B) Butan-1-ol

The correct decreasing order of their boiling points is:
questions.question:
Consider the following compounds of comparable molar mass:
(A) Propanoic acid
(B) Butan-1-ol
(C) Butanal
(D) Pentane

The correct decreasing order of their boiling points is:
questions.solution:
The boiling point of a compound depends on the strength of its intermolecular forces. All four compounds have comparable molar masses (ranging from $72$ to $74\text{ g/mol}$).

Propanoic acid (A) forms strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds and can exist as a cyclic dimer, leading to the highest boiling point.

Butan-1-ol (B) also exhibits intermolecular hydrogen bonding, but it is less extensive and weaker than that in carboxylic acids.

Butanal (C) possesses dipole-dipole interactions but lacks the ability to form intermolecular hydrogen bonds, resulting in a lower boiling point than the alcohol.

Pentane (D) is a non-polar molecule and only experiences weak London dispersion forces, giving it the lowest boiling point.

Thus, the correct decreasing order of boiling points is (A) > (B) > (C) > (D).

Answer: (A) > (B) > (C) > (D)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An aromatic hydrocarbon $A$ with molecular formula $\text{C}_9\text{H}_{12}$ is oxidized by hot alkaline $\text{KMnO}_4$ followed by acidification to give a tribasic acid $B$. Nitration of $B$ with an $\text{HNO}_3/\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ mixture yields only a single mononitro derivative $C$. The total number of $\pi$-bonds in one molecule of product $C$ is
questions.question: An aromatic hydrocarbon $A$ with molecular formula $\text{C}_9\text{H}_{12}$ is oxidized by hot alkaline $\text{KMnO}_4$ followed by acidification to give a tribasic acid $B$. Nitration of $B$ with an $\text{HNO}_3/\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ mixture yields only a single mononitro derivative $C$. The total number of $\pi$-bonds in one molecule of product $C$ is
questions.solution:
The formation of a tribasic acid $B$ upon oxidation implies that hydrocarbon $A$ has three oxidizable alkyl side chains. Since $A$ has the formula $\text{C}_9\text{H}_{12}$, it must be a trimethylbenzene.

The three isomers of trimethylbenzene are $1,2,3$-trimethylbenzene, $1,2,4$-trimethylbenzene, and $1,3,5$-trimethylbenzene. Upon oxidation, they yield the corresponding benzenetricarboxylic acids.

Nitration of $B$ yields only a single mononitro derivative $C$. This indicates that all available ring positions in $B$ are equivalent by symmetry. Only $1,3,5$-benzenetricarboxylic acid possesses such symmetry (positions 2, 4, and 6 are identical).

Therefore, $B$ is $1,3,5$-benzenetricarboxylic acid, and $C$ is $2$-nitrobenzene-$1,3,5$-tricarboxylic acid.

The total number of $\pi$-bonds in $C$ is calculated as follows:
Benzene ring: $3$ $\pi$-bonds
Three $-\text{COOH}$ groups: $3 \times 1 = 3$ $\pi$-bonds
One $-\text{NO}_2$ group: $1$ $\pi$-bond
Total $\pi$-bonds $= 3 + 3 + 1 = 7$.

Answer: $7$

Nitration of $B$ yields only a single mononitro derivative $C$. This indicates that all available ring positions in $B$ are equivalent by symmetry. Only $1,3,5$-benzenetricarboxylic acid possesses such symmetry (positions 2, 4, and 6 are identical).

Therefore, $B$ is $1,3,5$-benzenetricarboxylic acid, and $C$ is $2$-nitrobenzene-$1,3,5$-tricarboxylic acid.

One $-\text{NO}_2$ group: $1$ $\pi$-bond
Total $\pi$-bonds $= 3 + 3 + 1 = 7$.

Answer: $7$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following two isomeric carboxylic acids:
I. Pentanoic acid
II. 2,2-Dimethylpropanoic acid

Choose the correct relationship regarding their boiling points and solubilities in water.
questions.question:
Consider the following two isomeric carboxylic acids:
I. Pentanoic acid
II. 2,2-Dimethylpropanoic acid

Choose the correct relationship regarding their boiling points and solubilities in water.
options: Boiling point: I > II ; Solubility in water: I > II
Boiling point: II > I ; Solubility in water: II > I
Boiling point: I > II ; Solubility in water: II > I
Boiling point: II > I ; Solubility in water: I > II
questions.solution:
Boiling point depends on the surface area of the molecule. Pentanoic acid (I) is a straight-chain isomer with a larger surface area, leading to stronger van der Waals forces and a higher boiling point. 2,2-Dimethylpropanoic acid (II) is highly branched and more spherical, which decreases its surface area and van der Waals forces, resulting in a lower boiling point.

Solubility in water depends on the size and shape of the hydrophobic alkyl group. The branched and compact hydrophobic group in II causes less disruption to the hydrogen-bonded network of water compared to the extended straight chain in I. Therefore, the branched isomer (II) is more soluble in water than the straight-chain isomer (I).

Hence, the correct relationship is Boiling point: I > II and Solubility in water: II > I.

Answer: Boiling point: I > II ; Solubility in water: II > I

Consider the following reaction sequences that yield carboxylic acids as major organic products:
(A) $\mathrm{PhMgBr} + \mathrm{CO}_{2} \xrightarrow{\text{Dry ether}} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H}_{3}\mathrm{O}^{+}}$ Product A
(B) $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{MgBr} + \mathrm{CO}_{2} \xrightarrow{\text{Dry ether}} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H}_{3}\mathrm{O}^{+}}$ Product B
(C) $\mathrm{ClCH}_{2}\mathrm{CN} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H}_{3}\mathrm{O}^{+}/\Delta}$ Product C
(D) $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{C}\equiv\mathrm{CH} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{KMnO}_{4}, \mathrm{H}^{+}/\Delta}$ Product D

Which of the given reaction sequences produces the major product with the highest $\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}$ value?
questions.solution:
Product A is benzoic acid ($\mathrm{PhCOOH}$).

Product B is propanoic acid ($\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{COOH}$).

Product C is chloroacetic acid ($\mathrm{ClCH}_{2}\mathrm{COOH}$).

Product D is acetic acid ($\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{COOH}$).

The acidic strength depends on the stability of the conjugate base. The $+\mathrm{I}$ effect of alkyl groups destabilizes the carboxylate ion, decreasing acidity. The ethyl group in propanoic acid has a stronger $+\mathrm{I}$ effect than the methyl group in acetic acid. The $-\mathrm{I}$ effect of chlorine makes chloroacetic acid the strongest. Benzoic acid is stronger than both acetic and propanoic acids due to the $\mathrm{sp}^{2}$ hybridized carbon of the phenyl ring attached to the carboxyl group.

Order of acidic strength: Chloroacetic acid $>$ Benzoic acid $>$ Acetic acid $>$ Propanoic acid.

Since $\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}$ is inversely proportional to acidic strength, the weakest acid (propanoic acid) will have the highest $\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}$ value. Thus, Reaction (B) produces the product with the highest $\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}$.

Answer: Reaction (B)

The total number of hydrogen atoms in one molecule of the final product R is _______.
questions.question:
Consider the following sequence of reactions:
Ethylbenzene $\xrightarrow[\text{(ii) }\text{H}_3\text{O}^+]{\text{(i) }\text{KMnO}_4\text{, KOH, }\Delta}$ P $\xrightarrow{\text{SOCl}_2}$ Q $\xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{, Pd/BaSO}_4}$ R
The total number of hydrogen atoms in one molecule of the final product R is _______.
questions.solution:
(i) Ethylbenzene undergoes side-chain oxidation with alkaline $\text{KMnO}_4$ followed by acidification to form benzoic acid (Compound P).

(ii) Benzoic acid reacts with $\text{SOCl}_2$ to form benzoyl chloride (Compound Q).

(iii) Benzoyl chloride undergoes Rosenmund reduction with $\text{H}_2$ and $\text{Pd/BaSO}_4$ to form benzaldehyde (Compound R).

The chemical formula of benzaldehyde is $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO}$ (or $\text{C}_7\text{H}_6\text{O}$).

Therefore, the total number of hydrogen atoms in one molecule of R is $5 + 1 = 6$.

Answer: $6$

questions.q: An unknown alkyl nitrile 'A' undergoes complete hydrolysis to form a carboxylic acid 'B'. Compound 'B' is then treated with bromine and red phosphorus followed by water workup, yielding $2$-bromo-$3$-methylbutanoic acid as the major product. The IUPAC name of the starting alkyl nitrile 'A' is:
questions.question: An unknown alkyl nitrile 'A' undergoes complete hydrolysis to form a carboxylic acid 'B'. Compound 'B' is then treated with bromine and red phosphorus followed by water workup, yielding $2$-bromo-$3$-methylbutanoic acid as the major product. The IUPAC name of the starting alkyl nitrile 'A' is:
questions.solution:
Step 1: The final product is $2$-bromo-$3$-methylbutanoic acid, which is formed by the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction of carboxylic acid 'B'. The HVZ reaction selectively introduces a bromine atom at the $\alpha$-carbon.
Working backwards, replacing the $\alpha$-bromine with a hydrogen atom gives the structure of 'B' as $3$-methylbutanoic acid ($CH_3-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-COOH$).

Step 2: Carboxylic acid 'B' is formed by the complete hydrolysis of alkyl nitrile 'A'.
Replacing the carboxyl group ($-COOH$) with a nitrile group ($-C\equiv N$) gives the structure of 'A' as $CH_3-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-C\equiv N$.
The IUPAC name of this compound is $3$-methylbutanenitrile.

Answer: $3$-Methylbutanenitrile

(D) $\text{Aniline} \xrightarrow[\text{(ii) } \mathrm{CuCN}]{\text{(i) } \mathrm{NaNO}_{2}, \mathrm{HCl}, 0-5^{\circ}\mathrm{C}} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H}_{3}\mathrm{O}^{+}/\Delta} \text{Product D}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Product A: Diazotization of $p$-toluidine followed by Sandmeyer reaction with $\mathrm{CuCN}$ gives $p$-tolunitrile, which on hydrolysis yields $p$-toluic acid.

Product B: Similar reactions on $o$-toluidine yield $o$-toluic acid.

Product C: Reimer-Tiemann reaction of phenol yields salicylaldehyde as the major product. Oxidation of the aldehyde group by Tollens' reagent followed by acidification gives salicylic acid.

Product D: Aniline undergoes similar reactions to yield benzoic acid.

Comparing acidic strengths:
Salicylic acid (C) is the strongest acid due to the stabilization of its conjugate base (salicylate ion) via intramolecular hydrogen bonding.
$o$-Toluic acid (B) is stronger than benzoic acid due to the ortho effect, where steric hindrance forces the carboxylate group out of the plane of the benzene ring, reducing the destabilizing resonance from the ring.
Benzoic acid (D) is stronger than $p$-toluic acid (A) because the $p$-methyl group exerts $+\mathrm{I}$ and hyperconjugation effects, which destabilize the carboxylate anion.

Therefore, the correct decreasing order of acidic strength is (C) $>$ (B) $>$ (D) $>$ (A).

Answer: (C) $>$ (B) $>$ (D) $>$ (A)

Both isomers give an immediate white precipitate when warmed with alcoholic $\text{AgNO}_3$, and both yield benzoic acid upon vigorous oxidation with acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$. questions.question: Two isomers A and B have the molecular formula $\text{C}_9\text{H}_{11}\text{Cl}$. Both isomers give an immediate white precipitate when warmed with alcoholic $\text{AgNO}_3$, and both yield benzoic acid upon vigorous oxidation with acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$. Isomer A is optically active, while isomer B is optically inactive. The structures of isomers A and B respectively are:
questions.solution:
Oxidation of both isomers A and B with acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$ yields benzoic acid. This indicates that both isomers contain a single alkyl side chain attached to an unsubstituted benzene ring.

Since both isomers give an immediate white precipitate with alcoholic $\text{AgNO}_3$, the chlorine atom must be highly reactive, which is characteristic of benzylic or tertiary alkyl halides.

The molecular formula is $\text{C}_9\text{H}_{11}\text{Cl}$, which means the side chain has 3 carbon atoms.

Isomer A is optically active, meaning it has a chiral carbon. The structure that fits these criteria is 1-chloro-1-phenylpropane, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{CH}(\text{Cl})\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$.

Isomer B is optically inactive and must also be a highly reactive benzylic/tertiary halide. The only structure fitting this is 2-chloro-2-phenylpropane, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{C}(\text{Cl})(\text{CH}_3)_2$.

Answer: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{CH}(\text{Cl})\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{C}(\text{Cl})(\text{CH}_3)_2$
